methodological_rigor.justification: This is a single-center retrospective cohort of 894 HER2-negative mGC patients randomly split 8:2 into training (n=714) and internal validation (n=180) cohorts. The Cox regression univariate-to-multivariate approach, bootstrap validation (1000 resamples), time-dependent ROC, calibration, and DCA comparisons against multiple prior models are methodologically appropriate for nomogram development. However, the lack of external validation is explicitly acknowledged as a 'major limitation', the 8:2 internal split is weak (not a truly held-out cohort), and a priori exclusion of variables with >50% missingness (including PD-L1 CPS, EBV DNA, TMB) limits the model. Sensitivity analyses adjusted for confounders are a positive element.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The question is clinically important: first-line PD-1 blockade is now standard for HER2-negative mGC and individualized risk stratification is lacking. The nomogram uses routinely available variables (ECOG PS, pleural/peritoneal metastases, Lauren type, CRP, LDH) making it deployable in resource-limited settings. Discrimination is moderate (AUC 0.71-0.78) and stratification meaningfully separates PFS/OS and DCR, giving plausible clinical utility once externally validated. This is a retrospective cohort prognostic model, Oxford LoE 2b.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD applies for this prognostic prediction model. Most TRIPOD items are covered: participants, predictors, outcome definitions, missing-data handling, model development, performance (discrimination and calibration), risk group assignment, and head-to-head comparisons. The manuscript does not cite TRIPOD explicitly and omits several items (presentation of full multivariable model coefficients in main text, formal clinical usefulness thresholds, full handling of missing data beyond exclusion). A web-based dynamic nomogram is mentioned but URL is redacted. No formal data/code availability statement is present in the extracted text.

novelty_literature.justification: The authors position this as the first nomogram specific to HER2-negative mGC receiving first-line PD-1 blockade, which is a meaningful niche given the recent shift in standard of care (CheckMate-649, ORIENT-16, RATIONALE-305, KEYNOTE-859). The individual predictors (ECOG PS, effusion, CRP, LDH, Lauren) are all previously reported, and prior prognostic indices (mGPS, GIPI, RMH, JCOG) exist. The contribution is a meaningful combination plus benchmarking in the first-line immunotherapy era, modest rather than transformative.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly structured with explicit cohort definition, reproducible statistical methods, and a balanced discussion that acknowledges the key limitations (single center, no external validation, >50% missingness of molecular markers, PD-L1 as a predictive not pure prognostic marker). Tables are detailed, though Table 1 and Table 2 are densely formatted in the markdown. Minor language issues but overall communication is clear and professional.

key_strengths: Largest reported single-center cohort (n=894) of HER2-negative mGC on first-line PD-1 blockade
Appropriate survival modeling with bootstrap internal validation, calibration, and decision curve analyses
Head-to-head benchmarking against PD-L1 CPS, mGPS, GIPI, RMH and JCOG indices showing consistent superiority
Predictors are routinely available in clinical practice, supporting real-world deployability
Sensitivity analyses adjusting for multiple confounders
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design with internal random-split validation only; no true external validation
Moderate discrimination (AUC ~0.68-0.78) limits personalized prediction accuracy
A priori exclusion of variables with >50% missingness (PD-L1 CPS, EBV DNA, TMB) may omit informative biology
Study is prognostic rather than predictive; without a comparator arm the incremental value over standard clinical assessment is difficult to quantify
TRIPOD checklist not explicitly addressed; no formal data/code availability statement
Pleural/peritoneal effusion grading relies on radiologist judgment with acknowledged variability
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a solid but incremental single-center retrospective nomogram study with moderate discrimination and no true external validation, fitting tier 3 journals (e.g., ESMO Open scope at upper end, otherwise Cancers/BMC Cancer). Reporting improvements and clearer handling of missingness would justify minor revisions at that tier.
